a.selection: 3 intervals, each at least1200bp,3 distinct proper-clade sets, minimum internal branch>2.5%maxage
a.meaning: A genuine5-sample recorded ARG is shown as3 wireframe marginal-tree slices. Unary nodes collapse in both source/destination, recombination diamonds appear at original recorded times on source branches only. Faint longitudinal guides join the same retained ARG node within this one simulated genealogy. These do not imply persistent inferred internal-node identities in the model.
a.sampling_ages: All5samples are time0. Isometric floor/baselines follow each projected tip baseline. Slanted depth is a layout coordinate, not sampling age.
a.matching: Identical tree drawing function and shared node coordinates, times and planar leaf orders generate a/b, transformed only by width and isometric slant. Markers omitted from b do not alter branches.
a.interval_encoding: solid gray, diagonal hatch, crosshatch used consistently on ARG baseline, genomic strip and extracted-tree header strips

recombination_detail.meaning: msprime record_full_arg stores the two ancestral material lineages of this same recombination as paired nodes9/10, with identical event time and same child. The detail co-locates these records as biological eventR and draws their genuine older parents. It is a topology magnification, not a new simulated node, invented genealogy or common-time-scale inset.
recombination_detail.links: Dashed leaders connect detailR to its original per-interval branch markers. The3marginal trees and their coordinates are unchanged.

b.meaning: All5tip genotypes are observed. Four neutral reference circles supply actual source badges Ana/CHG/WHG/EHG. The magenta outlined q1 square has '?' ancestry. Magenta tracks one sample's identity across trees/memory/readout. Ancestry hues are reserved for reference badges and outputs. This tiny illustration exemplifies4references+1query and does not depict the production panel size.
b.omitted_from_drawn_vector: MLP also uses sample ages, observed donor/panel allele frequencies and callability. Internal nodes carry observed age/root/sample role. Edge gates depend on observed branch geometry and mutation concordance.
b.variant_columns: The3actual hypothetical variant-site positions are marked on the genomic strip. Each tip's3allele columns carry matching interval hatching. They are a compact illustration of the observed genotype input, not a numerical rendering of every model feature. Interval-specific site encoding/pooling is performed by encode_sites.
b.reference_vectors: Below every known ancestry badge a4component one-hot input is drawn. The query has4empty ancestry slots and an explicit unknown badge, without masking alleles.

ancestor_vector.graphic: [tau,0,0] attached to a real internal nonroot node in T2
ancestor_vector.meaning: Observed age, root indicator0, sampled indicator0. Both binary components are0, so the manuscript's sampled/root ordering gives the same correct glyph. No known ancestry feature is attached to ancestors.
ancestor_vector.assertion: Generator asserts the depicted node has a parent, has children, and is not sampled.

b.schematic_values: Displayed feature cells and supplied reference-label examples are schematic. Underlying toy allele columns derive from hypothetical mutations on this illustrative simulated ARG, not scientific observations or fitted model features.

c.meaning: Both complete up/down traversals use identical learned weights and gates. A traversal is level-wise message passing until every native node has been visited, not an arbitrary fixed number of graph hops. Downward outside messages exclude the recipient contribution. Repeated modules are the final architecture, not development variants. Up→Down order is explicit via stage arrows inside each GNN.
c.base_residual: The original base is bypassed to the plus symbol. First-pass states generate node-local and memory injections, which are added to the original base before the second traversal.

node_update.meaning: Rank8 gained/lost proper-clade feature residual, does not gather another tree's learned state
Rank8 own-state residual on eligible clade representatives, not foreign episode information

memory.meaning: At the observed350-generation cut, projection of first-pass upward+outside context gives per-cut-group forcing. Forcing is assigned to each persistent sample. Bidirectional span-decay scans follow the same sample columns. Directions are averaged, pooled over current cut groups, centered by subtracting current forcing, then projected back to width32 and injected at cut representatives. This mechanism precedes and differs from the final BiGRU.
memory.graphic_abstraction: 5aligned sampled rows are shown in every memory matrix. Faint bidirectional links preserve each reference row, while magenta q1 shows span-dependent rho gates and current-force sum. μ denotes current-cut-group pooling. A small representative-node glyph explicitly lies on the injection path. The diagram summarizes both scans and the final centered/projected readout; it does not add a GRU or another model variant.
memory.gate: rho=exp(-native interval span / learned ell). Current forcing enters with1-rho in code. Both directions use these physical-span weights.

shapes.drawn_notation: N_t x d for all native model nodes, S x d per tree for aligned sampled states. d=32 in actual implementation.
shapes.matrix_encoding: Generic blue-gray varied feature cells,5 stable sample rows with magenta q1 row outline. No class or sample labels are encoded by cell color.

c.leaf_projection: Concatenate per-sample upward/outside states, Linear64to32 then tanh. It is not whole-graph pooling.
c.weight_sharing: Dashed bracket links the two GNN boxes and is labeled same weights. It is independent of the solid base residual arrow, which has a visible source junction on node features and a terminal arrow into the plus node.
c.sample_row_readout: Each Sxd matrix has5rows and a highlighted q1row. A connected highlighted vector from the row is labeled e_tq. All sample rows undergo the same processing, with q1traced as the output example.

d.meaning: One-layer bidirectional GRU takes per-tree, per-haplotype context plus log-scaled span and neighboring interval-center distances:35input,32hidden per direction. All sampled haplotype rows are processed. Classifier sees local32 and recurrent64 context, then Linear96to32/GELU/Linear32to4. Query selection is at readout. No concatenation of whole graph embeddings occurs.

schematic_output.reason: q1 remains sister to the WHG reference in all3true marginal trees. A stable WHGexample is biologically interpretable despite changing surrounding genealogy. These values are not model predictions or empirical results.
schematic_output.connection: A short downward arrow connects probability bars to the discrete interval-wise argmax strip.

d.separate_memory: BiGRU is a final genomic readout, not the persistent-sample memory that is injected before traversal2.
d.genomic_geometry_glyph: Grayscale hatched3-interval glyph feeds BiGRU. Its span/neighbor distances are described in caption rather than equations in the figure.
d.local_recurrent_join: A visible matrix-output junction branches into the BiGRU and the lower local embedding bypass. Local and recurrent paths meet at the explicit circled Vert concatenation symbol immediately before the final MLP. This concatenates same-haplotype local32 and recurrent64 feature vectors, not graph embeddings.
